durable_task_continuation.checkpoint_rule: After a meaningful gate, evidence, approval, handoff, workspace, progress, or continuation change, the Supervisor may validate and persist the next revision. A native interruption does not invalidate the last persisted revision.
durable_task_continuation.reference_rule: Evidence, receipts, and handoffs are referenced by stable locator and optional digest; their payloads are not duplicated in the checkpoint.
invariants: Task state and checkpoint revision belong to the Supervisor.
Native worker session and thread state belong to the worker or Bridge and are replaceable.
Changing last_execution must not change task identity, completed gates, or evidence references.
Canonical JSON is the only accepted serialized representation.
No model-generated prose, event log, advisory memory, or worker self-report is authoritative checkpoint state.
The contract is worker-neutral and has no external orchestrator dependency.
Persistence transport and automatic respawn, classification, and retry execution are outside ASR-1.
Classification is pure, deterministic, idempotent, worker-neutral, and does not mutate the checkpoint.
Normal session completion on an open task continues to the next phase and is not a retry.
Human-required and review-required outcomes are never eligible for automatic resume, same-worker retry, or reroute.
Eligibility fields are classifications only; this gate performs no resume, retry, reroute, session spawn, bridge call, timing, or daemon behavior.
Unknown, absent, or contradictory non-overridden evidence requires review.
No model prose or provider-specific failure branch is accepted as termination evidence.
The classifier has no external orchestrator dependency.

eligibility: ASR-2 classification is resumable or retry_same_worker_candidate and exposes automatic-resume or same-worker-retry eligibility
approval is neither pending nor rejected
source worker and native session ids are present
same_worker_respawn.acknowledgement: A host supplies a non-empty native session id different from the source. A matching first acknowledgement advances checkpoint revision and retry count and installs the new running session; an exact duplicate is idempotent and a mismatch is rejected.
invariants: Planning and acknowledgement are pure state operations and perform no transport or spawning.
The claim key is deterministic and contains no clock, randomness, provider, or model data.
The source native session is reference-only and is never a target session.
Task identity, gates, and evidence, receipt, and handoff references survive acknowledgement.
No new native session id is invented by policy code.
The implementation has no external orchestrator dependency.

invariants: Only pass sets execution_allowed true.
Unknown effects are reconciled before replay and applied mutations are not replayed.
Read-only replay is allowed only from explicit read_only metadata.
The deterministic spawn-plan claim key prevents the same host action from executing twice for either ASR-3 or ASR-5.
Preflight is pure and idempotent and mutates neither checkpoint nor plan.
Preflight performs no filesystem read, Bridge call, spawn, effect, acknowledgement, timer, or daemon behavior.

cross_worker_recovery.acknowledgement: A host supplies a new native session id for the selected target worker. Exact duplicate acknowledgement is idempotent; stale, mismatched, same-worker, unsupported-target, or reused-source-session transitions are rejected.
invariants: The source worker is injected into existing routing failed_workers so it cannot be immediately selected again.
Selection reuses existing capability, availability, quota, and task-shape policy.
The deterministic recovery claim key contains no clock or randomness.
ASR-4 preflight gates stale state, human or safety blocks, workspace drift, ambiguous effects, applied mutations, and duplicate claims before host execution.
Planning and acknowledgement preserve durable checkpoint material and perform no transport, spawn, effect, filesystem read, timer, or daemon behavior.
The implementation has no external orchestrator dependency.

live_supervisor_host.persistence: checksummed envelope, exclusive temporary create, file sync, atomic rename, directory sync
live_supervisor_host.claiming: one exclusive host lock per checkpoint path
invariants: Supervisor task identity remains stable across native session lineage changes.
Every host transition increments one deterministic sequence and an acknowledgement records a receipt.
Malformed or checksum-mismatched checkpoints fail closed.
Bridge observations normalize above unchanged Bridge tool surfaces.
Unknown lifecycle or effect facts fail closed.
LSH-2 performs no replacement worker spawn.
LSH-3 executes only a preflight-passed ASR-3 same-worker plan through an existing Bridge tool.
Unknown spawn acknowledgement enters reconciliation and is never blindly replayed.
LSH-4 executes only a preflight-passed ASR-5 plan and delegates target choice to selectWorker.
The source and previously acknowledged lineage workers are excluded and reroute count is bounded.
Accepted spawn evidence is reconciled after restart without issuing a duplicate spawn.
LSH-6 proves real Pi-source and Claude-source interruption followed by policy-selected cross-worker continuation into fresh, exactly observed Codex native sessions.

LSH-6 uses disposable read-only Git fixtures, stable task identity, LSH-1-through-LSH-5 continuation context, durable deterministic claims and receipts, and bounded retry state with no fixture mutation.
Unresolved reconciliation, approvals, safety blocks, corrupt state, and exhausted budgets require a human.
Concurrent host claims are excluded and demonstrably stale PID locks are recoverable.
The Supervisor Host is not a fourth worker.
The Supervisor Host is not a liveness daemon.
The runtime imports worker-neutral policy only and does not import Bridge implementation code.
Closed LSH gates qualify the on-demand Host paths recorded here; they do not introduce Bridge changes, a background liveness daemon, or a deployed always-on Supervisor service.
